title: Securely Configuring AWS Services with Phoenix Protocol
objectives: Avoid hallucinated tools and dynamic IDs

mission_brief.situation: You are operating in a controlled cloud sandbox environment where actions must be repeatable and auditable.
mission_brief.mission: Perform secure cloud operations using real AWS CLI commands.
mission_brief.execution: Follow each lab step carefully and validate results using deterministic output techniques.

content.concept: In this lesson, you will learn how to securely configure various AWS services using the Phoenix Protocol. This includes setting up IAM roles, configuring VPCs, and securing EC2 instances. By the end of this lesson, you should be able to confidently deploy secure cloud infrastructure using the Phoenix Protocol.
content.walkthrough: To begin, navigate to the AWS Management Console and select the account that you wish to configure. Then, go to the IAM dashboard and create a new role with the necessary permissions. Next, move on to the VPC dashboard and set up a new VPC with appropriate subnets and security groups. Finally, launch an EC2 instance with the correct AMI and configure its security settings.
common_mistakes: Incorrectly configuring IAM roles can lead to unnecessary exposure of sensitive data.
Failing to properly secure EC2 instances can result in unauthorized access.
Ignoring VPC settings can compromise network security.

lab.setup: Use a sandbox AWS account. Never run these commands in production.
steps: Create a new AWS account and log in to the AWS Management Console.
Navigate to the IAM dashboard and create a new role with the necessary permissions.
Go to the VPC dashboard and set up a new VPC with appropriate subnets and security groups.
Launch an EC2 instance with the correct AMI and configure its security settings.
Verify that all services are properly configured and secure.

elite_competence.role_simulation: You are responsible for ensuring every action can be audited and repeated reliably.

bug_injection.bug: Validation relied on a random AWS-generated ID.
bug_injection.symptom: Learners cannot pass the lab even when the command is correct.
bug_injection.fix: Validate only stable fields using --query and --output text.

interrogation_questions: What are some common mistakes to avoid when configuring IAM roles?
How do you ensure that EC2 instances are properly secured?
What are the key considerations for setting up VPCs?

legal_context.allowed: Authorized training activities conducted in sandbox environments only.
legal_context.prohibited: Any unauthorized access, production usage, or violation of cloud provider terms is strictly forbidden.

resume_bullets: Executed deterministic AWS CLI security operations
Validated outputs using stable query techniques
